metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 190. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.text: vaṃśe jātaḥ savitur anaghe mānayan mānuṣatvaṃ devaḥ śrīmāñ janakatanayānveṣaṇe jāgarūkaḥ
children.translated_text: Born in the stainless lineage of the Sun, the glorious god, honoring his human state, remained vigilant in the search for <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter.

children.text: pratyāyāte pavanatanaye niścitārthaḥ sa kāmī kalpākārāṃ kathamapi niśām ā vibhātaṃ viṣehe ||
children.translated_text: When the son of the Wind had returned and the matter was certain, that love-stricken one somehow endured a night like an aeon until dawn.

children.text: kālye senāṃ kapikulapates tūrṇam udyojayiṣyan dūrībhāvāj janakaduhitur dūyamānāntarātmā
children.translated_text: At daybreak, wishing quickly to set in motion the army of the monkey-king, his inner self tormented by the distance of <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter,

children.text: krīḍākhelaṃ kamalasarasi kvāpi kālopayātaṃ rākācandradyutisahacaraṃ rājahaṃsaṃ dadarśa ||
children.translated_text: he saw, somewhere at a lotus lake, a royal swan that had come at the right time, moving in playful sport and accompanied by the splendor of the full moon.

children.text: tasmin sītāgatim anugate taddukūlāṅkamūrtau tanmañjīrapratimaninade nyastaniṣpandadṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: Upon it, which seemed to follow <s>Sita</s>'s way, whose form bore the mark of her garment, and whose sound resembled that of her anklet, he fixed an unmoving gaze.

children.text: vīraś cetovilayam agamat tanmayātmā muhūrtaṃ śaṅke tīvraṃ bhavati samaye śāsanaṃ mīnaketoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hero, his self absorbed in her, for a moment underwent a dissolution of mind. I think the command of the fish-bannered Love is severe at its proper time.

children.text: labdhāśvāsaḥ kathamapi tadā lakṣmaṇasyāgrajanmā saṃdeśena praṇayamahatā maithilīṃ jīvayiṣyan
children.translated_text: Then the elder brother of <s>Laksmana</s>, somehow recovering his breath, wishing to keep <s>Maithili</s> alive by a message rich in affection,

children.text: cakre tasmai sarasijadalaiḥ sopacārāṃ saparyāṃ kāntāśleṣād adhikasubhagaḥ kāmināṃ dūtalābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: performed for that swan a respectful worship with lotus petals. For lovers, obtaining a messenger is more fortunate than an embrace by the beloved.

children.text: kṛtvā tasmin bahumatim asau bhūyasīm āñjaneyād gāḍhonmādaḥ praṇayapadavīṃ prāpa vārtānabhijñe
children.translated_text: Having shown the swan very great regard, greater than toward <s>Anjaneya</s>, he, deeply maddened and not knowing the news, entered the path of supplication born of love.

children.text: viśleṣeṇa kṣubhitamanasāṃ meghaśailadrumādau yācñādainyaṃ bhavati kimuta kvāpi saṃvedanārhe ||
children.translated_text: For those whose minds are disturbed by separation, there is abject entreaty even toward clouds, mountains, trees, and the like; how much more toward something fit to feel awareness.

children.text: vedodanvadvibhajanavido vaṃśajaṃ viśvamūrter āhuḥ siddhāḥ kamalavasater aupavāhyaṃ bhavantam
children.translated_text: The perfected beings say that you are descended from the universal-formed one who knew how to divide the ocean of the Veda, and that you are the mount of the lotus-dwelling one.

children.text: labdhaṃ yena praguṇagatinā tatpriyāyāḥ sakāśāt tatsāvarṇyaṃ śravaṇarasanāsvādayogyā sudhā ca ||
children.translated_text: By your excellent gait you have obtained from that beloved of his both similarity of color and nectar fit to be tasted by ears and tongues.

children.text: madhye kecit vayam iha sakhe kevalaṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ vyaktotkarṣo mahati bhuvane vyomagānāṃ patis tvam
children.translated_text: Friend, here we are merely among human beings; you are lord of those who go through the sky, with manifest excellence in the great world.

children.text: sthāne dūtyaṃ tad api bhavataḥ saṃśritatrāṇahetoḥ sarvasraṣṭā vidhir api yataḥ sārathitvena tasthau ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this mission is fitting for you, for the sake of protecting those who have sought refuge; for even <s>Vidhi</s>, the creator of all, once stood in the role of charioteer.

children.text: icchāmātrāj jagad aparathā saṃvidhātuṃ kṣamāṇām ikṣvākūṇāṃ prakṛtimahatām īdṛśīṃ prekṣya velām
children.translated_text: Seeing this limit of the <s>Ikshvaku</s>s, whose majestic nature is capable of arranging the world otherwise by mere wish,

children.text: lakṣyālakṣye jaladhipayasā labdhasaṃsthāṃ trikūṭe laṅkāṃ gantuṃ tava samucitaṃ rākṣasīṃ rājadhānīm ||
children.translated_text: it is proper for you to go to <s>Lanka</s>, the demonic capital, established on <s>Trikuta</s> amid the visible and invisible waters of the ocean.

children.text: sthānair divyair upacitaguṇāṃ candanāraṇyaramyāṃ muktāsūtiṃ malayamarutāṃ mātaraṃ dakṣiṇāśām
children.translated_text: The southern quarter is enriched by divine places, lovely with sandal forests, a source of pearls, and mother of the winds from <s>Malaya</s>.

children.text: asmatprītyai janakatanayājīvitārthaṃ ca gacchann ekaṃ rakṣaḥpadam iti sakhe doṣaleśaṃ sahethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Going for our pleasure and for the life of <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter, friend, you should bear this slight fault: that it is a single abode of demons.

children.text: vācālānām iva jaḍadhiyāṃ satkavau dūrayāte kailāsāya tvayi gatavati kṣībatām āśritānām
children.translated_text: When you have gone to <s>Kailasa</s>, as a good poet leaves behind the talkative dull-witted, those intoxicated with pride will be far away.

children.text: saṃmodas te pathi pariṇamec candrakair ujjhitānāṃ meghāpāye vipinaśikhināṃ vīkṣya vācaṃyamatvam ||
children.translated_text: On your path, your joy will mature when you see the forest peacocks, deprived of their moon-spotted plumes after the clouds have passed, keeping silence.

children.text: āraktānāṃ navamadhu śanair āpiban padminīnāṃ kālonnidre kuvalayavane ghūrṇamānaḥ salīlam
children.translated_text: Gently drinking the fresh honey of the reddened lotuses, moving playfully in the blue-lotus grove awakened by time,

children.text: svinno dānair vipinakariṇāṃ saumya seviṣyate tvām āmodānām ahamahamikām ādiśan gandhavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fragrant wind, moist with the rut-fluid of forest elephants, gentle one, will serve you, directing a contest among aromas.

children.text: paryāptaṃ te pavanacalitair aṅgarāgaṃ parāgaiḥ sthāne kuryuḥ samasamudayād bandhavo bandhujīvāḥ
children.translated_text: Your kinsmen, the bandhujiva flowers, will rightly make enough cosmetic coloring for you with pollen stirred by the wind, because of their simultaneous blooming.

children.text: yenānviṣyasy acalatanayāpādalākṣānuṣaktaṃ cūḍācandraṃ puravijayinaḥ svarṇadīphenapūrṇam ||
children.translated_text: With that coloring you will search out the crescent moon on the head of the city-conqueror, filled with foam from the golden river and tinged with the lac from the feet of the mountain's daughter.

children.text: sūkṣmākārair dinakarakaraiḥ kalpitāntaḥśalākāḥ śāropāntāḥ śatamakhadhanuḥśeṣacitrāṃśukena
children.translated_text: The autumn clouds, with inner rods fashioned by the subtle rays of the sun, their edges white, and with cloth variegated by the remnant of <s>Satamakha</s>'s bow,

children.text: ūḍhāḥ paścād ucitagatinā vāyunā rājahaṃsachatrāyeran nabhasi bhavataḥ śāradā vārivāhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: carried afterward by the wind moving in due course, will become like royal-swan parasols for you in the sky.

children.text: drakṣyasy evaṃ priyasakha sukhaṃ laṅghitādhvā sakhīṃ te sītāṃ kṣetre janakanṛpater utthitāṃ sīrakṛṣṭe
children.translated_text: Thus, dear friend, having happily crossed the road, you will surely see your friend <s>Sita</s>, arisen in the field of King <s>Janaka</s> when the furrow was drawn by the plough.

children.text: gopāyantī tanum api nijāṃ yā kathaṃcin madarthaṃ bhūmau loke vahati mahatīm ekapatnīsamākhyāṃ ||
children.translated_text: She somehow preserves even her body for my sake, and in the world on earth bears the great title of the one-wife vow.

children.text: prakṣīṇāṃ tvadvirahasamaye jātaharṣām idānīṃ pratyāyāsyann anunaya śanaiḥ padminīṃ svāduvācā
children.translated_text: When she, wasted away during the time of separation from you, is now born into joy, as you return, gently conciliate that lotus-lady with sweet speech.

children.text: sā te tantrīsvanasubhagayā syād itīhābhyanujñāṃ manye kuryān madhukaragirā maithilīsauhṛdena ||
children.translated_text: I think that she, with friendship for <s>Maithili</s>, would here give you permission in the voice of bees, made lovely by the sound of lute-strings.

children.text: sārdhaṃ kāntaiḥ śabarasudṛśām adrikuñjeṣu rāgād āsīnānāṃ kṣaṇam asamaye dṛśyacandrodayaśrīḥ
children.translated_text: At the wrong time, the beauty of moonrise may be seen for a moment in mountain bowers where the beautiful-eyed <s>Sabara</s> women sit passionately with their lovers.

children.text: uḍḍīyethāḥ sarasijavanād dakṣiṇāśānusārī paśyan dūrāt prabalagarutāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ dattavartmā ||
children.translated_text: Fly up from the lotus grove, following the southern quarter, watching from afar the path granted by the birds with powerful wings.

children.text: aṅgīkurvann amṛtarucirām utpatiṣṇoḥ salīlaṃ chāyām antas tava maṇimayo mālyavān eṣa śailaḥ
children.translated_text: As you rise gracefully, this jeweled mountain <s>Malyavan</s>, accepting within itself your moon-bright shadow,

children.text: śobhāṃ vakṣyaty adhikalalitāṃ śobhamānām atīndor devasyāder upajanayato mānasād indubimbam ||
children.translated_text: will declare a more charming beauty, like the face of the primal god, which produces the moon's disk from its mind.

children.text: mārgau samyaṅ mama hanumatā varṇitau dvau tayos te sahyāsanno 'py anaghasubhagaḥ paścimo nityavarṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Two roads have been properly described to me by <s>Hanumat</s>; of these, though near the <s>Sahya</s>, the western one, stainless and lovely, is always rainy.

children.text: prācīneṣu pratijanapadaṃ saṃhatāv adbhutānāṃ magnā dṛṣṭiḥ katham api sakhe matkṛte te nivāryā ||
children.translated_text: On the eastern route, in every district there is a cluster of marvels; friend, your gaze, though somehow sunk in them, must be restrained for my sake.

children.text: śrutvā śabdaṃ śravaṇamadhuraṃ tāvakaṃ pāmarīṇāṃ pratyāsannāt sapadi bhavanāt sādaraṃ nirgatānām
children.translated_text: Hearing your sound, sweet to the ear, the village women will respectfully come out at once from their nearby houses.

children.text: abhrūbhaṅge 'py adhikasubhagair niścitāṅgaḥ kaṭākṣair deśān etān vanagirinadīsaṃvibhaktān vyatīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even if your brows are slightly bent, with glances made more lovely by that, you should pass over these regions, whose parts are distinctly divided by forests, mountains, and rivers.

children.text: ikṣucchāye kisalayamayaṃ talpam ātasthuṣīṇāṃ saṃlāpais tair muditamanasāṃ śālisaṃrakṣikāṇām
children.translated_text: There, the women guarding the rice-fields have taken up beds made of fresh shoots in the shade of the sugarcane,

children.text: karṇāṭāndhravyatikaravaśāt karbure gītibhede muhyantīnāṃ madanakaluṣaṃ maugdhyam āsvādayethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, their minds delighted by such conversations, they are bewildered by a mottled variety of song produced by the mingling of Karṇāṭa and Āndhra styles; you should savor their innocent charm, clouded by love.

children.text: viṣṇor vāsād avanivahanād baddharatnaiḥ śirobhiḥ śeṣaḥ sākṣād ayam iti janaiḥ samyag unnīyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Because it is the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and because the earth is borne by jewel-bound heads, people correctly infer, 'This is <s>Śeṣa</s> himself.'

children.text: abhrair yukto laghubhir acironmuktanirmokakalpair agre bhāvī tadanu nayane rañjayann añjanādriḥ ||
children.translated_text: Joined with light clouds that seem like recently cast-off sloughs, <s>Añjanādri</s> will appear before you, afterwards delighting your eyes.

children.text: tatrārūḍhair mahati manujaiḥ svargibhiś cāvatīrṇaiḥ sattvonmeṣād vyapagatamithastāratamyādibhedaiḥ
children.translated_text: There, among men who have climbed that great mountain and gods who have descended, differences such as mutual superiority and inferiority have disappeared through the blossoming of pure being.

children.text: sādhāraṇyāt phalapariṇateḥ saṃghaśo badhyamānāṃ śaktyā kāmaṃ madhuvijayinas tvaṃ ca kuryāḥ saparyām ||
children.translated_text: Since the fruit that comes to maturity is common to all, groups gather there; you too should, as far as you are able, freely perform worship of the conqueror of <s>Madhu</s>.

children.text: stokonmagnasphuritapulināṃ tvannivāsecchayeva drakṣyasyārāt kanakamukharāṃ dakṣiṇām añjanādreḥ
children.translated_text: Nearby, south of <s>Añjanādri</s>, you will see the gold-resounding river, with sandbanks only slightly risen, as if through a wish that you should dwell there.

children.text: āsannānāṃ vanaviṭapināṃ vīcihastaiḥ prasūnāny arcāhetor upaharati yā nūnam ardhendumauleḥ ||
children.translated_text: With wave-hands she surely offers flowers, for the sake of worship of the crescent-crested lord, from the forest trees standing nearby.

children.text: nirviśyāināṃ nibhṛtam anabhivyaktamañjupraṇādo mandādhūtaḥ pulinapavanair vañjulāmodagarbhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having quietly enjoyed her, while the sweet sounds are not openly manifest, and while she is gently stirred by breezes from the sandbanks carrying the fragrance of vañjula blossoms,

children.text: avyāsaṃgaḥ sapadi padavīṃ saṃśrayānyair ala?ghyo bandīkuryus taṭavasatayo mā bhavantaṃ kirātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then quickly take to the road, without attachment and difficult for others to transgress, lest the hunters dwelling on the bank make you captive.

children.text: tuṇḍīrākhyaṃ tadanu mahitaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vīkṣamāṇaḥ kṣetraṃ yāyāḥ kṣapitaduritaṃ tatra satyavratākhyam
children.translated_text: Then, while beholding the honored district called <s>Tuṇḍīra</s>, go to the sin-destroying sacred field there named <s>Satyavrata</s>.

children.text: patyau roṣāt salilavapuṣo yatra vāgdevatāyāḥ setur jajñe sakalajagatām ekasetuḥ sa devaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There that god, the one bridge for all the worlds, became a bridge when the goddess of speech, in watery form, was angry with her lord.

children.text: nānāratnair upacitaguṇāṃ nityasaṃgītanādāṃbhūmer drakṣyasy ucitavibhavaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ tatra kāñcīm
children.translated_text: There you will see <s>Kāñcī</s>, the fittingly splendid ornament of the earth, enriched with manifold jewels and filled with constant music.

children.text: yasyāṃ nityaṃ nihitanayano hastiśailādhivāsī dvandvātītaḥ sa khalu puruṣo dṛśyate satyakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that city the true-willed person, beyond all dualities, dwelling on <s>Hastiśaila</s>, is seen with his eyes ever fixed upon it.

children.text: tām āsīdan praṇama nagarīṃ bhaktinamreṇa mūrdhnā jātām ādau kṛtayugamukhe dhātur icchāvaśena
children.translated_text: Approaching that city, bow to it with your head bent in devotion, for it was first created at the beginning of the Kṛta age according to the will of the creator.

children.text: yadvīthīnāṃ karigiripater vāhavegāvadhūtān dhanyān reṇūṃs tridaśapatayo dhārayanty uttamā?gaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The blessed dust of its streets, shaken up by the speed of the lord of <s>Karigiri</s>'s vehicle, is borne on their highest heads by the lords of the gods.

children.text: mandādhūtāt tadanu mahito niḥsṛtaś cūtaṣaṇḍāt pārśve tasyāḥ paśupatiśiraścandranīhāravāhī
children.translated_text: Then, from a grove of mango trees, gently stirred and honored, there will surely come forth beside that city a fragrant wind carrying the cool mist of the moon on <s>Paśupati</s>'s head.

children.text: dūrāt prāptaṃ priyasakham iva tvām upaiṣyaty avaśyaṃ kampāpāthaḥkamalavanikākāmuko gandhavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That wind, a lover of the lotus groves in the waters of the <s>Kampā</s>, will approach you from afar like a dear friend who has arrived.

children.text: varṇastomair iva pariṇatā saptabhedair mahāughair mānyā madhyenagaram abhitaḥ sevitā devatābhiḥ
children.translated_text: As though matured into masses of colors, with its sevenfold great streams, honored and attended on all sides in the middle of the city by deities,

children.text: svacchasvāduprasarasubhagā svāminī vaḥ kavīnāṃ vegāsaṃjñāṃ vahati mahatīṃ vallabhā padmayoneḥ ||
children.translated_text: clear, sweet, flowing, and beautiful, the mistress of poets, beloved of the lotus-born god, bears the great name <s>Vegā</s>.

children.text: tīrthe puṃsāṃ śamitakaluṣe tatra sārasvatākhye snātvā sārdhaṃ munibhir anaghaiḥ samyag ullāsitā?gaḥ
children.translated_text: At that tīrtha (sacred bathing place) called <s>Sārasvata</s>, where men's impurity is calmed, bathe together with sinless sages, your limbs properly refreshed.

children.text: viśvaṃ citte vigatarajasi vyañjayantīm aśeṣaṃ vakṣyasy antar bahir api parāṃ śuddhim akṣepaṇīyām ||
children.translated_text: Then you will proclaim an unimpeachable supreme purity, both inward and outward, revealing the whole universe in a mind free from passion.

children.text: tasyās tīre sarasijabhuvaḥ saumya vaitānavedir divyaṃ kurvan draviḍaviṣayaṃ dṛśyate hastiśailaḥ
children.translated_text: On her bank, gentle one, <s>Hastiśaila</s> is seen as the divine sacrificial altar of the lotus-born god, sanctifying the Drāviḍa land.

children.text: yasyopānte kṛtavasatayo yāpayitvā śarīraṃ vartiṣyante vitamasi pade vāsudevasya dhanyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Near it, blessed people who have made their dwelling there, after passing through the body, will live in the darkness-free abode of <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: saṃcinvānā taruṇatulasīdāmabhiḥ svām abhikhyāṃ tasyāṃ vedyām anuvidadhatī śītalaṃ havyavāham
children.translated_text: On that altar the world-mother, the goddess, gathers her own beauty with garlands of young tulasī and imitates a cool sacrificial fire.

children.text: bhogāiśvaryapriyasahacaraiḥ kﾔ āpi lakṣmīkaṭākṣair bhūyaḥ śyāmā bhuvanajananī devatā saṃnidhatte ||
children.translated_text: She is made yet darker by the wondrous sidelong glances of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, accompanied by beloved enjoyment and sovereignty, and she is present there.

children.text: lakṣmīvidyullalitavapuṣaṃ tatra kāruṇyapūrṇaṃ mā bhaiṣīs tvaṃ marakataśilāmecakaṃ vīkṣya megham
children.translated_text: There, when you see the cloud dark like emerald stone, with a form lovely with the lightning of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and full of compassion, do not be afraid.

children.text: śuddhair nityaṃ paricitapadas tvādṛśair devahaṃsair haṃsībhūtaḥ sa khalu bhavatām anvavāyāgrajanmā ||
children.translated_text: For he, familiar always with the pure paths of divine swans like you, has become a swan himself; he is indeed the first-born ancestor of your lineage.

children.text: sārāsvādī savanahaviṣāṃ svāminas te sa devaḥ śuddhaṃ cakṣuḥ śrutipariṣadāṃ cakṣuṣāṃ bhāgadheyam
children.translated_text: That god, your lord, who relishes the essence of the oblations at the soma-pressings, is the pure eye of the assemblies of the Veda and the good fortune of all eyes.

children.text: a?gīkuryād vinatam amṛtāsārasaṃvādibhis tvām āvirmodair abhimatavarasthūlalakṣaiḥ kaṭākṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: May he accept you as you bow, with glances whose manifest delights resemble streams of nectar and whose broad marks confer desired boons.

children.text: madhvāsaktaṃ sarasijam iva svinnam ālambamāno devyā hastaṃ taditarakaranyastalīlāravindaḥ
children.translated_text: If that glorious god, holding the goddess's hand moist like a lotus attached to honey, while a playful lotus is placed in his other hand,

children.text: devaḥ śrīmān yadi sa viharet svairam ārāmabhūmau vyakto vālavyajanavapuṣā vījayes taṃ tvam eva ||
children.translated_text: should roam freely in the pleasure garden, then you yourself, appearing in the form of a yak-tail fan, should fan him.

children.text: jātaprītir janapadam athﾒ o madhyamaṃ la?ghayitvā dūrāllakṣyakramukanivahaśyāmalān yāhi colān
children.translated_text: Then, having grown pleased and having crossed the middle country, go to the <s>Cola</s> lands, dark from afar with rows of areca palms.

children.text: pratyudgacchanmakaravalanastambhitaiḥ sahyajāyāḥ srotobhedair vividhagatibhiḥ saṃvibhaktāvakāśān ||
children.translated_text: Their spaces are divided by the streams of the daughter of the <s>Sahya</s>, flowing in various courses, checked by banks of makaras that come out to meet them.

children.text: saṃdhyārāgaṃ surabhirajanīsaṃbhavair a?garāgaiḥ keśair jyotsnātimirakalahaṃ pālikāpīḍagarbhaiḥ
children.translated_text: There the red of twilight is matched by fragrant night-born unguents, and the quarrel of moonlight and darkness is held within coiffures heavy with pālikā ornaments.

children.text: ābibhrāṇāḥ sarasijadṛśo haṃsa dolādhirohād ādhāsyante madakalagiras teṣu netrotsavaṃ te ||
children.translated_text: Lotus-eyed women, climbing onto swings, will set a festival for your eyes among them, O swan, with voices sweet and intoxicated.

children.text: pṛthvīlīlātilakasubhagaṃ paścimaṃ bhāgam eṣāṃ nāmnā varṣaṃ jalacara nadīmātṛkaṃ gāhamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Entering the western part of these regions, charming as the play-ornament of the earth, a land named for rivers as its mothers, O water-going one,

children.text: drakṣyasy ārāt parimitatayā magnakailāsadṛśyaṃ śvetaṃ śailaṃ phaṇipatim iva kṣmātalād ujjihānam ||
children.translated_text: you will see nearby, because of its limited size, the white mountain, appearing like Kailāsa sunk down, rising up from the surface of the earth like the lord of serpents.

children.text: sphārālokapraśamitatamaḥsaṃcayaṃ tatra puṃsāṃ pratyagrūpaṃ praguṇavibhavaṃ prārthanīyaṃ budhānām
children.translated_text: There, a divine radiance, with its ample light calming accumulated darkness, fresh in form, rich in fitting splendor, and desirable to the wise,

children.text: nedīyāṃsaṃ kuśalanivahaṃ nantur ādhāsyate te divyaṃ tejo jaladhitanayāsnehanityānuṣaktam ||
children.translated_text: being very near, will bestow upon you, when you bow, a mass of welfare; it is ever attached by affection to the daughter of the ocean.

children.text: snigdhacchāyaṃ tadanu vitataṃ tasya dhāmﾒ ￪va nīlaṃ nīlīpuṣpastabakalalitaṃ kānanaṃ saṃvicīyāḥ
children.translated_text: After that, you should examine the broad dark-blue forest, as though it were the blue radiance of that abode, cool with dense shade and lovely with clusters of nīlī flowers.

children.text: dṛṣṭe tasminn animiṣavadhūnityanirveśayogye svargodyānaśriyam api laghuṃ maṃsyate mānasaṃ te ||
children.translated_text: When it is seen, your mind will think even the beauty of heaven's gardens slight, for it is fit to be enjoyed constantly by the wives of the immortals.

children.text: kurvan nānākusumarajasā yatra citraṃ vitānaṃ pūgāraṇye mṛdu vicalayan pālikācāmarāṇi
children.translated_text: There the wind, making a many-colored canopy with the pollen of various flowers and gently moving the chowries of areca groves,

children.text: pādanyāsakṣamam avakiran kṣmātalaṃ puṣpajālaiḥ prāyo vāyuḥ parijanavidhiṃ pañcabāṇasya dhatte ||
children.translated_text: scattering nets of flowers over the ground fit for the placing of feet, generally performs the service of an attendant for Pañcabāṇa, the god of love.

children.text: srotovegād atha janapadaṃ saumya sīmantayantī pratyādeśo vibudhasaritaḥ syandate sahyakanyā
children.translated_text: Then, O gentle one, marking off the country with the speed of her current, the daughter of the Sahya mountain flows along, a rival command to the river of the gods.

children.text: kāle kāle pariṇativaśāt parvabhedāvakīrṇaiḥ puṇḍr￪kṣūṇāṃ pulinaviśadair gadgadā mauktikāughaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At each proper season she is choked with streams of pearls, bright as sandbanks, scattered from heaps of puṇḍra sugarcane through the changes of ripening and the breaking of joints.

children.text: sahyotsaṃgāt sapadi marutā sāgaraṃ nīyamānāṃ bhadrālāpair vihitakuśalāṃ tvādṛśānāṃ dvijānām
children.translated_text: From the lap of Sahya she is quickly carried by the wind toward the ocean; with auspicious sounds she has arranged welfare for twice-born beings such as you.

children.text: yām askannāḥ sarasakuhalīpatrapātair niśānte mandasmerāṃ madhuparimalair vāsayantﾒ ￮va pūgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At dawn, the areca trees, smiling faintly with honeyed fragrance, perfume her as their fresh, moist pollen-bearing leaves fall without interruption.

children.text: tasmin drakṣyasy amaramahilāmauligandhair avandhyām ātanvānāṃ vyapagatarasaṃ mānase mānasaṃ vaḥ
children.translated_text: There you will see the wealth of a Puṣkariṇī, made fruitful by the fragrances from the hair of immortal women, spreading a mind in your mind after all weariness is gone.

children.text: tīrthair anyair api parigatāṃ śuddhihetoḥ samantāccandrollāsaprathitayaśasaḥ saṃpadaṃ puṣkariṇyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is surrounded on every side by other sacred bathing places for the sake of purification, and its fame is made manifest by the moon's shining beauty.

children.text: tīre tasyā viracitapadaṃ sādhubhiḥ sevyamānaṃ śraddhāyogād vinamitatanuḥ śeṣapīṭhaṃ bhajethāḥ
children.translated_text: On its bank, bowing your body with devotion, you should approach the Śeṣapīṭha, whose place has been established there and which is served by holy people.

children.text: yasminn asmatkuladhanatayā saumya sāketabhājaḥ sthānaṃ bhāvyaṃ munibhir uditaṃ śrīmato ra?gadhāmnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that place, O gentle one, sages have declared that there is the destined seat of the glorious abode of Raṅga, cherished as the treasure of our lineage, for those who dwell in Sāketa.

children.text: satve divye svayam udayatas tasya dhāmnaḥ prasa?gān mañjūṣāyāṃ marakatam iva bhrājamānaṃ tadantaḥ
children.translated_text: Because that divine being's abode has manifested by itself, inside it shines like an emerald in a casket,

children.text: ceto dhāvaty upahitabhujaṃ śeṣabhoge śayānaṃ dīrghāpā?gaṃ jaladhitanayājīvitaṃ devam ādyam ||
children.translated_text: and the mind runs toward the primal god, the life of the daughter of the ocean, lying on the couch of Śeṣa with his arm set upon it and with long sidelong glances.

children.text: corākrāntaṃ tadanu vipinaṃ colapāṇḍyāntarasthaṃ jhillīnādaśravaṇaparuṣaṃ śīghram eva vyatīyāḥ
children.translated_text: After that, quickly pass through the forest between the Cola and Pāṇḍya lands, overrun by thieves and harsh to the ear with the sound of crickets.

children.text: tīrṇe tasmin prakaṭaya sakhe śītalāṃs te ninādān śabdāyante na khalu kavayaḥ saṃnidhau durjanānām ||
children.translated_text: When that has been crossed, friend, make your cool notes heard; poets, indeed, do not sound forth in the presence of wicked people.

children.text: srastāpīḍapracaladalakaṃ vyaktatāṭa?karatnaṃ muktācūrṇasphuritatilakaṃ vaktraṃ uttānayantyaḥ
children.translated_text: In that region, blue-lotus-eyed women, raising their faces with loosened head-ornaments, trembling curls, visible jeweled earrings, and tilaka marks sparkling with pearl-powder,

children.text: deśe tasmin kuvalayadṛśo jātakautūhalās tvāṃ mālādīrghair madhuravirutaṃ mānayiṣyanty apā?gaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: will honor you, curious about you, with long garland-like sidelong glances as you sing sweetly.

children.text: nityāvāsaṃ vṛṣabham acalaṃ sundarākhyasya viṣṇoḥ pratyāsīdan sapadi vinato bhāgadheyaṃ nataḥ syāḥ
children.translated_text: Drawing near at once to Vṛṣabha, the immovable eternal dwelling of Viṣṇu called Sundara, you should bow down and be blessed by that good fortune.

children.text: yasyﾒ otsaṃge balivijayinas tasya mañjīravāntaṃ pātho divyaṃ paśupatijaṭāsparśahīnaṃ vibhāti ||
children.translated_text: On its slope shines the divine water that murmurs at the anklets of that conqueror of Bali, untouched by the matted hair of Paśupati.

children.text: īśād astrāṇy adhigatavatāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ prabhāvāt kārāvāsasmaraṇacakitaiḥ siktasasyān payodaiḥ
children.translated_text: Because of the might of kṣatriyas who had obtained weapons from Īśa, the rain clouds, frightened by the memory of imprisonment, have watered the crops.

children.text: paśyan yāyāḥ param alakayā spardhamānair ajasraṃ puṇyāvāsaiḥ purajanapadair maṇḍitān pāṇḍyadeśān ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the Pāṇḍya lands adorned continually with meritorious villages and towns that rival Alakā, you should proceed onward.

children.text: muktājālair janitapulināṃ śuktisaṃtānamuktais tārāpūrṇaṃ divam iva tatas tāmraparṇīṃ bhajethāḥ
children.translated_text: Then you should resort to the Tāmraparṇī, whose sandbanks are formed by nets of pearls released from lines of oysters, like the sky filled with stars.

children.text: pratyāsattyā niyataviśadaṃ pītasindhor maharṣeḥ pānīyaṃ te pariṇamayitā tatra muktāmayatvam ||
children.translated_text: There, through nearness, the always clear water of the ocean drunk by the great sage will transform you into something pearl-like.

children.text: tasyāḥ svairaṃ sarasijamukhāsvādasaṃprītacetāḥ śītībhūtas taralalaharībāhusaṃśleṣaṇena
children.translated_text: With your mind freely delighted by tasting lotus-faces, cooled by the embrace of her arms of restless waves,

children.text: adhyāsīnaḥ pulinam anilair vījitaś candanādreḥ śrāntiṃ śāntiṃ gamayatu bhavān sāgaraṃ la?ghayiṣyan ||
children.translated_text: seated on her sandbank and fanned by winds from the sandal mountain, may you bring your fatigue to rest and peace before crossing the ocean.

children.text: savyaṃ tasyāḥ kiyad iva gataḥ śyāmatālītamālāṃ tvatprāyāṇāṃ taruṇavayasāṃ cetaso nandayitrīm
children.translated_text: After going a little to her left, you will see nearby the shore of the ocean, dark with rows of palm and tamāla trees, delighting the minds of young ones such as you,

children.text: velām abdher vividhalaharīdattamuktābhirāmāṃ drakṣyasy ārād dviguṇapulināṃ ketakīnāṃ parāgaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: lovely with pearls given by varied waves, and with its sandbanks doubled by the pollen of ketakī flowers.

children.text: sthitvā tatra kṣaṇam ubhayataḥ śailaśṛ?gāvatīrṇaiḥ srotobhedair adhigataguṇaṃ cāruviṣphāraghoṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: Standing there for a moment, with streams descending on both sides from the mountain peaks and made excellent by their lovely spreading roar,

children.text: lakṣyīkurvan daśamukhapurīṃ saumya patraprakṛṣṭo velācāpaṃ śara iva sakhe vegatas tvaṃ vyatīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: take Laṅkā, the city of Daśamukha, as your target; driven on by your wings, O gentle friend, speed past the ocean-shore as an arrow crosses a bow.

children.text: dāvāsaktaṃ vanam iva nabhaḥ saṃdhyayﾔ ￪vānuviddhaṃ sindūrā?kaṃ dvipam iva hariṃ svāmbareṇﾒ ￪va juṣṭam
children.translated_text: The sky appears as if pierced by twilight like a forest caught by wildfire, and the lion, marked with vermilion like an elephant, seems attended by its own garment.

children.text: vidyudbhinnaṃ ghanam iva sakhe vidrumāraṇyayogād dehenāikaṃ mithunam iva ca drakṣyasi tvaṃ payodhim ||
children.translated_text: Friend, from its union with forests of coral, you will see the ocean as if it were a cloud split by lightning, and also as if it were a single pair united in one body.

children.text: asmatpūrvaiḥ surapatihṛtaṃ draṣṭukāmais tura?gaṃ bhitvā kṣoṇīm agaṇitabalaiḥ sāgaro vardhitātmā
children.translated_text: Wishing to see the horse stolen by the lord of the gods from our ancestors, <s>Sagara</s>, whose self had grown vast through his innumerable mighty sons, split open the earth.

children.text: satkārārthaṃ tava yadi girīn ādiśed guptapakṣān aśrānto 'pi praṇayam ucitaṃ nāiva bandhor vihanyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, for the sake of honoring you, he should command the mountains whose wings are hidden, then, though you are not weary, you should not reject the proper affection of a kinsman.

children.text: tatrāsīnaḥ kva cana sarasi smerahemāravinde labdhāsvādo madhubhir amitaiḥ saṃvinītādhvakhedaḥ
children.translated_text: Sitting there somewhere on a lake with smiling golden lotuses, having found delight in countless kinds of honey, and having had the fatigue of the road thoroughly calmed,

children.text: drakṣyasy agre laghutaragatiḥ śeṣam ulla?ghya sindhos toyāghātān masṛṇitaśilāramyavelaṃ suvelam ||
children.translated_text: you will see ahead, after crossing the remainder of the ocean with swifter motion, <s>Suvela</s>, whose lovely shore is adorned with rocks smoothed by the beating of the waters.

children.text: yasyāsanne payasi jaladhes tvatpraticchandacandrāḥ pakṣacchedakṣaritarudhirastomasaṃdarśanīyāḥ
children.translated_text: In the water of the sea near it, the corals, with moonlike reflections of you, look as though they show heaps of blood flowing from the cutting of wings.

children.text: vīcīprāpter viṣamitaruco mauktikais tārakābhaiḥ saṃdhyām anyāṃ niyatam avanau darśayanti pravālāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the waves reach them, their radiance is broken up by pearls like stars; surely they display upon the earth another twilight.

children.text: yatrāraṇyaṃ varuṇavasater vīcivegāpanītair muktāratnastabakaśabalair vidrumair utpravālam
children.translated_text: There the forest at the abode of <s>Varuna</s> is made luxuriant with corals carried away by the force of the waves and variegated with clusters of pearl-gems,

children.text: rakṣobhītaiḥ svayam animiṣair āhṛtasthāpitānāṃ mandārāṇāṃ madhuparimalair vāsitaṃ maulidaghnaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and it is perfumed with the honey-fragrance of mandara flowers, head-high, brought and set there by the unblinking gods themselves in fear of the demons.

children.text: tasmin dṛśyā bhavati bhavataś cārusaudhāvadātā la?kā sindhor mahitapuline rājahaṃs￮va līnā
children.translated_text: On that honored sandbank of the ocean, <s>Lanka</s>, white like beautiful palaces, appears to you as if she were a royal swan resting there.

children.text: tvām āyāntaṃ pavanataralair yā patākāpadeśaiḥ pakṣair abhyujjigamiṣur iva sthāsyati śrāvyanādā ||
children.translated_text: As you come, with the pretext of banners trembling in the wind as her wings, she will stand as though wishing to fly up to meet you, while her sound is audible.
